title: HF privileges and band slices
blurb: Which HF bands and slices a General may use, which modes are barred, and what secondary status means.

G1A01.why: Extra-only slices exist on **80, 40, 20 and 15 m**. The other HF and MF bands are open to General across the band.
G1A01.trap: 160, 60, 30, 17, 12 and 10 m have no Extra-only slice.

G1A02.why: Phone is prohibited on **30 m**, which is limited to non-voice modes.

G1A03.why: Image transmission is prohibited on **30 m**, as is phone.

G1A05.why: **7.125 to 7.175 MHz** is in 40 m's Extra-only slice. The 15 m and 10 m ranges listed are open to General.
G1A05.trap: 21.275 to 21.300 and 28.000 to 28.025 are General frequencies.

G1A06.why: Secondary: **do not cause harmful interference** to primary users, and **accept** their interference.
G1A06.trap: No call sign recording, emergency-only or time-of-day rule applies.

G1A07.why: General class may use CW on the **entire 10 m band**, 28.000 to 29.700 MHz.

G1A08.why: Extra-exclusive segments exist on **80, 40, 20 and 15 m**.

G1A09.why: 21.300 MHz (21300 kHz) is on **15 m** and outside the Extra slice. 14250 is 20 m, 18155 is 17 m, 24900 is 12 m.
G1A09.trap: The other three are not on 15 m at all.

G1A10.why: 10 m repeaters belong in the part **above 29.5 MHz**.

G1A11.why: Extra holds the bottom of a shared voice segment, so General gets the **upper** frequency portion.
G1A11.trap: It is the upper portion on every band, not a mix.
